result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers advise against brand-derived status colors and flag that the brand red on buttons clashes with 'failed'. A goes further, with exact hex values for text and fill, icons and labels, a failed red set apart from the button red, and contrast estimates it openly says still need checking. B names hues only and offers hex values later, so it is less complete and a little wordier. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reject purely on-brand status colors, spot the conflict between the brand red and the button color, and require icons and labels as well as color. B is the better answer because it gives concrete hex values for each status's badge text and fill, and it handles readability properly: it uses dark amber text, says the contrast figures are estimates that need checking, and flags that dark mode needs separate values. B's Running blue (#1d6fd1 on #e8f1fc) looks closer to about 4.3:1 than 5:1, but B said its numbers were unmeasured. A only names hues and offers to supply hex values later.
